skill.description: Guides authorized red-team and bug bounty workflows for reconnaissance, discovery, web testing, API enumeration, and finding documentation.

skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: This community skill is a dual-use red-team guide with many runnable reconnaissance, fuzzing, and vulnerability scanning workflows. Several Markdown fence detections are false positives, but command blocks and network examples present real misuse risk without strict authorization controls. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Dual-use red-team workflow can be applied outside authorized scope.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit refusal guidance for unsanctioned targets and require written authorization, scope, rate limits, and program rules before active testing.

remediation.issue: Runnable active scanning and fuzzing commands lack built-in guardrails.
remediation.suggestion: Separate passive and active steps, add approval checkpoints, include safe concurrency defaults, and warn users before running network-heavy tools.

remediation.issue: Automated XSS and API probing examples can test production systems.
remediation.suggestion: Limit payload examples to authorized labs or in-scope assets, and require manual validation before reporting any scanner result.

remediation.issue: The automated recon script accepts arbitrary domains.
remediation.suggestion: Add scope validation, logging, dry-run guidance, and rate-limit configuration before presenting the script as an executable workflow.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid DoS or fuzzing on production without permission
- Rate limit requests to avoid blocking

content.value_statement: Security teams need repeatable reconnaissance without losing scope discipline. This skill organizes authorized red-team and bug bounty workflows into practical steps.
actual_capabilities: Maps a staged workflow for acquisition research, ASN lookup, subdomain enumeration, and live host discovery.
Lists command examples for Amass, Subfinder, httpx, httprobe, ffuf, Nuclei, Dalfox, and waybackurls.
Provides manual analysis questions for files, APIs, profiles, integrations, error pages, and authorization boundaries.
Includes a Bash reconnaissance script outline for subdomains, live hosts, URL collection, and Nuclei scans.
Offers quick references for web testing tools, API endpoints, XSS filter checks, and troubleshooting.
limitations: Requires explicit authorization and scope before any active testing.
Assumes a Linux security workstation and installed third-party tools.
Uses placeholder domains that users must adapt to program rules and laws.
Automated scan results require manual validation before disclosure.

use_cases.title: Plan Bug Bounty Reconnaissance
use_cases.description: Build a scoped workflow for passive discovery, live host checks, content discovery, and finding triage.

use_cases.title: Structure Internal Assessments
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable checklist for authorized application mapping, API review, vulnerability scanning, and evidence collection.

use_cases.title: Teach Web Testing Methodology
use_cases.description: Use the tool list and workflow sections to teach responsible reconnaissance and validation practices.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Authorized Recon
prompt_templates.prompt: I have written authorization to test example.com. Build a scoped reconnaissance plan using this skill. Include inputs, tools, outputs, and rate limits.

prompt_templates.title: Create Enumeration Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a subdomain and live-host enumeration checklist for an approved bug bounty target. Put passive steps before active steps.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Web Testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these allowed assets and technologies. Prioritize content discovery, API checks, and XSS testing by risk and effort.

prompt_templates.title: Design Safe Recon Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an authorized recon pipeline for multiple domains. Include storage layout, tool order, validation steps, rate limits, and report-ready artifacts.

output_examples.input: Plan first-day reconnaissance for an authorized bug bounty program covering example.com.
output: A scoped plan that starts with passive discovery and acquisition research.
A separate active phase for live host checks, content discovery, and controlled scanning.
A validation phase for duplicate removal, false positive review, and report preparation.

output_examples.input: Prioritize testing for an approved web application with APIs, profiles, and file uploads.
output: A risk-ranked checklist covering file uploads, API authorization, profile fields, integrations, and error pages.
Suggested evidence to collect for each finding type.
Notes to avoid out-of-scope testing and production disruption.

output_examples.input: Turn scanner output into a responsible bug bounty report outline.
output: A concise finding summary, affected assets, reproduction steps, impact statement, and remediation guidance.
A reminder to remove false positives and avoid unsupported severity claims.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, target scope, rate limits, and prohibited techniques before active testing.
Run passive discovery before active probing, then document each tool, input, output, and timestamp.
Manually verify automated findings before disclosure, and remove duplicates or false positives from reports.
anti_patterns: Testing domains, IPs, or subsidiaries that are not explicitly in scope.
Running fuzzing or vulnerability scans without rate limits or production safeguards.
Submitting scanner output without manual validation, reproduction steps, and impact analysis.

faq.question: Is this skill only for authorized testing?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it only with written authorization, defined scope, and program rules.

faq.question: Does the skill install tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It assumes tools such as Amass, Subfinder, httpx, ffuf, Nuclei, and Dalfox are already available.

faq.question: Can it run active scans?
faq.answer: It provides workflows for active scans, but users must approve commands and apply rate limits.

faq.question: Does it validate vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: It helps organize validation, but automated findings still require manual review and evidence.

faq.question: What targets should users provide?
faq.answer: Users should provide only in-scope domains, IP ranges, applications, and program restrictions.

faq.question: Is it suitable for training?
faq.answer: Yes, when used in labs, internal ranges, or authorized programs with clear safety rules.
